tools.name: search_threats
tools.description: Search OffSeq Radar's vulnerability and threat corpus (CVE records, CISA KEV, ENISA EUVD, EPSS, public exploits, news). Combine filters to answer questions like "exploited Fortinet CVEs this month" or "critical CVEs with rising EPSS". Results carry priority, KEV, EPSS, exploit maturity and EUVD sign

tools.name: get_threat
tools.description: One vulnerability or threat record by CVE id (e.g. CVE-2024-3400) or Radar slug, resolved to the authoritative record: CVSS, priority with its factors, CISA KEV, EPSS with 30-day history, exploit maturity and sources, ENISA EUVD, OffSeq Mirage, source consensus, affected versions and remediation.

tools.name: match_packages
tools.description: Check installed packages against known vulnerabilities with ecosystem-native version comparison (distro backports included). Each package is a purl with version (pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.20, pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u2?distro=bookworm), or name + ecosystem + version, or a CPE. Returns per pac

tools.name: scan_sbom
tools.description: Scan a whole SBOM or lockfile for vulnerable dependencies, riskiest first, with upgrade advice per package. Formats: cyclonedx-json, spdx-json, package-lock, composer-lock, cyclonedx-xml, spdx-tag-value, yarn-lock, pnpm-lock, cargo-lock, uv-lock, poetry-lock, gemfile-lock, go-mod, go-sum, purl-list,

tools.name: prioritize_cves
tools.description: Rank 2 to 50 CVEs into a patch order using Radar's priority score (CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV, ransomware, exploit maturity, exploited but not in CISA KEV). Each row says why it ranks above the next; patterns group CVEs sharing a product, vendor or weakness.

tools.name: check_iocs
tools.description: Look up indicators of compromise (IP addresses, domains, URLs, file hashes) in the indicators Radar extracted from threat reports. Matching is a case-insensitive substring match per indicator type; up to 5 threats per indicator.

tools.name: check_eol
tools.description: End-of-life status of software versions from endoflife.date: per purl or CPE with a version (pkg:npm/vue@2.7.16, pkg:pypi/django@4.2.11, cpe:2.3:a:nodejs:node.js:18.20.4), the release cycle, its EOL date, days left and whether it is eol, near-eol (within windowDays) or supported.

tools.name: get_landscape
tools.description: What changed across the vulnerability landscape in a window: CISA KEV additions, exploitation not in KEV (ENISA EUVD, OffSeq Mirage), new public exploits, EPSS risers and new critical CVEs, plus CVEs that several of those name (multiSignal). Each panel cites its source and as-of time.

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: Your "What changed" feed: new signals (KEV listing, EPSS jump, exploit published, EUVD exploited, fix available...) on CVEs you starred or that affect your monitored hosts, plus decisions that went stale, expired or are due for review. Newest first.

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description: Hosts in your Radar inventory (registered by the threat-finder CLI) with each host's cached finding summary and an account-wide aggregate. Use list_host_findings for one host's findings.

tools.name: list_host_findings
tools.description: Current vulnerability findings for one of your hosts, riskiest first, with exposure, KEV, EPSS, fix versions and any decision you recorded. Get hostId from list_hosts.

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: Your decision ledger: what you decided per CVE (patch_now, defer, accept, not_affected, mitigated), the assumptions behind it, and whether it still holds (active, review_due, expired, stale when a signal broke an assumption, withdrawn when its CRA assessment no longer states a verdict).

tools.name: record_decision
tools.description: Record a decision about a CVE in your ledger. Radar re-checks the assumptions as signals change and flags the decision stale when one breaks. Verdicts: patch_now, defer (needs until), accept, not_affected and mitigated (take a VEX justification). Assumptions that do not hold today are rejected. Conf

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "record_decision" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Record a decision about a CVE in your ledger. Radar re-checks the assumptions as signals change and flags the decision stale when one breaks. Verdicts: patch_no…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "scan_sbom" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
